subject: Urgent: production latency + error surge — proposed cache intervention
messages:
From: Jenna Li <jenna@stellari.ai>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
Cc: support@stellari.ai
Date: Fri, 05 Dec 2026 09:12:43 -0800
Subject: Production: sudden latency & errors since 03:00 UTC

Hi Kimberly,

We started seeing a significant degradation in production starting ~03:00 UTC today. Main metrics: p95/p99 latency climbed from ~220ms/480ms to 1.1s/2.4s, overall error rate increased from 0.3% to ~6%, and observed throughput (requests/s) fell ~28%. We attached a small snapshot of token-level traces and the high-level metrics.

This is impacting our real-time customer feature (autocomplete). Can your team confirm whether this is a Redwood-side regression or something we need to mitigate locally? We briefly saw 502/504 spikes and a few 429s today.

Attachments: stellari-impact-snapshot-20261205.csv

Thanks — we’re on standby and can share additional logs.

— Jenna Li
CTO, Stellari
jenna@stellari.ai

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
To: Jenna Li <jenna@stellari.ai>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.ai, jonas_weber@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 05 Dec 2026 09:30:12 -0800
Subject: Re: Production: sudden latency & errors since 03:00 UTC

Hi Jenna — thanks for the quick heads-up and the snapshot. We’re treating this as high priority.

Preliminary notes from a quick check: there is a correlated rise in KV cache eviction rates for Stellari’s tenant and a corresponding increase in head-of-line (HOL) blocking on the hot lane. That pattern can cause exactly the latency + error profile you’re seeing when hot keys begin to thrash and batching windows extend.

Immediate actions we’d like to take (need your ok to proceed):
- Route Stellari traffic to an isolated priority pool for 30 minutes to stop cross-tenant interference (no customer-visible model change).
- Temporarily reduce max batch size for your tenant from 64 -> 8 to cut HOL wait time.
- Flush the tenant’s KV prefix cache and enable a short warmup window (10m).

If you approve, we will also enable our degraded-path fallback model (smaller, same quality tier) while we stabilize the cache. That should keep availability high while we make configuration changes.

We’ve looped in Ops (Jonas) and Sales (Ben) so we can coordinate messaging and commercial impacts. I’ll share a short remediation plan in the next email.

Attachments: —

— Kimberly Park
Senior Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference
kimberly_park@redwood.ai
From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 05 Dec 2026 10:05:37 -0800
Subject: Re: Production: sudden latency & errors since 03:00 UTC

Kimberly / Marissa — quick ops readout after pulling the runtime traces and KV metrics:

Findings:
- Stellari tenant shows sustained hot-key activity on a small set of prefixes (top 3 prefixes account for ~72% of cache hits).
- Eviction churn doubled in the last 2 hours; per-shard LRU windows are dropping live entries before reuse -> observed cache thrash.
- When a hot key misses, the request triggers a large batch that waits for slower members (HOL). Combined with KV miss penalty, p99 explodes.

Short-term mitigations (safe to apply now):
1) Pin Stellari to an isolated pool (dedicated slice) — immediate throughput isolation, quick rollback.
2) Reduce per-tenant max_batch_size to 8 and lower batch_wait_ms from 12 -> 4ms for the tenant’s routes.
3) Increase KV TTL for the tenant from default 30s -> 180s to reduce eviction churn for read-heavy prefixes.
4) Disable prefix-prefetch optimization for their tenant (it’s triggering prefetch storms at our current prefetch window).

Risks and rationale:
- Pinning to an isolated pool requires temporary capacity reservation; small burst (~2-3 GPUs) to avoid impacting other customers. We can use reserved burst pool for 45 minutes.
- Increasing TTL will raise memory pressure; we’ll monitor occupancy and revert if pressure exceeds 75%.

I recommend we apply 1+2 immediately (routing + batch size) and 3+4 if occupancy stays safe after 10m.

I’ll prepare a single-click playbook that ops can run; we should coordinate with Ben for external approval/notice.

— Jonas (Ops)
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 05 Dec 2026 10:27:04 -0800
Subject: Re: Production: sudden latency & errors since 03:00 UTC

All — I’m elevating to the engineering leadership path for exec visibility and fast approval. Proposed immediate action plan (what we execute now):

A. Technical mitigation (0-30m):
  1) Route Stellari to isolated priority pool (Jonas to run).
  2) Reduce tenant max_batch_size to 8 and batch_wait_ms -> 4ms (Jonas/infra).
  3) Flush the tenant KV prefix and start 10m warmup.
  4) Enable fallback small model for read-only autocomplete route (no change to ranking model).

B. Follow-up (30m-6h):
  1) Monitor cache occupancy and eviction rate; if occupancy > 70% revert TTL increase.
  2) Run targeted hot-key analysis and advise Stellari on key-shard distribution patterns (they may need client-side sharding).
  3) Provision a short reserved-burst capacity if traffic persists.

Commercial/exec ask: I authorize the technical steps above and recommend we offer Stellari a 10% credit for the incident window as goodwill. Ben — please prepare a short note and confirm.

I’ll join a quick sync in 15m if needed.

— Marissa Cole
Engineering Manager, Serving Runtime
marissa_cole@redwood.ai

Jenna / Oliver — summary of what we did and next steps: 

Actions taken (completed):
- We routed Stellari traffic to an isolated priority pool at 10:02 PST (automatic rollback in 45m).
- Reduced max_batch_size to 8 and batch_wait_ms to 4ms for your tenant at 10:05 PST.
- Flushed the tenant’s KV prefix cache and initiated a 10m warmup period at 10:07 PST.
- Standby fallback model enabled for the autocomplete route.

Immediate impact: p95/p99 latency dropped to ~260ms/520ms within 6 minutes and error rate fell back to ~0.45%. Throughput recovered to within 95% of baseline. We attached the incident snapshot and diagnostics.

Next steps we recommend together:
1) We’ll run a hot-key distribution report and share recommendations for client-side key sharding by EOD today.
2) If you agree, we’ll keep the isolated routing for another 45 minutes and then evaluate whether to make configuration changes permanent.
3) We will prepare a short post-incident report with timeline and mitigations; expect that within 24 hours.

Please reply with a quick OK on the isolated routing extension and permission for the post-incident credit.

Attachments: diagnostics-sysdump-20261205.tar.gz; stellari-impact-snapshot-20261205.csv

Thanks again for the rapid cooperation — we’ll keep monitoring and I’ll be available on Slack/phone.
